doc_title: IMS Clause Conformity Checklist — SQCDP / HESQ
title: IMS Clause Conformity Checklist — SQCDP / HESQ
instructions: Ready-to-use internal audit checklist covering all three standards, clause by clause.
Each clause is tagged against SQCDP (Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, People) and HESQ (Health, Environment, Safety, Quality) so an audit can be run along either lens.
Ref. Documents lists the controlled documents that declare that clause. A code in brackets is tagged to a different standard; NONE means no document declares it.
Mark C / NC / OFI / NA and record the objective evidence actually examined.
The same checklist runs live in Auditor Mode on the document portal.

blocks.title: Audit Lens
blocks.note: Tick the lens the audit is being run along. Filter the rows accordingly.

blocks.title: Clause Conformity Checklist
prefill: Are external and internal issues relevant to the QMS determined, monitored and reviewed?
Are interested parties and their relevant requirements determined and monitored?
Is the scope of the QMS documented, with any non-applicable clause justified?
Are the QMS processes, their sequence, interaction, criteria and measures defined?
Does top management demonstrate leadership - accountability, resources, promoting improvement?
Is the quality policy documented, communicated and available to interested parties?
Are roles, responsibilities and authorities assigned, communicated and understood?
Are risks and opportunities determined, with actions planned and their effectiveness evaluated?
Are quality objectives measurable, monitored, communicated and updated, with plans to achieve them?
Are changes to the QMS planned and carried out in a controlled manner?
Are the resources needed for the QMS determined and provided?
Are the persons necessary for effective operation of the QMS determined and provided?
Is infrastructure determined, provided and maintained (buildings, equipment, utilities)?
Is the environment for the operation of processes determined, provided and maintained?
Are monitoring and measuring resources suitable, calibrated, identified and safeguarded?
Is the organisational knowledge needed for processes determined and maintained?
Is competence determined, and are training and its effectiveness evaluated and recorded?
Are persons aware of the policy, objectives, their contribution and the implications of nonconformity?
Are internal and external communications on the QMS determined - what, when, with whom, how?
Is documented information controlled - identification, review, approval, version, distribution, retention?
Is operational planning and control implemented, including criteria, resources and retained records?
Is customer communication defined, including enquiries, contracts, feedback and complaints?
Are requirements for products and services determined, including statutory and regulatory?
Are requirements reviewed before commitment to supply, with records of the review?
Are changes to product requirements recorded and relevant persons made aware?
Are externally provided processes, products and services controlled to specified requirements?
Are external providers evaluated, selected, monitored and re-evaluated against defined criteria?
Is the type and extent of control over external providers defined and verified?
Is information communicated to external providers adequate before it is communicated?
Is production carried out under controlled conditions - documented information, monitoring, suitable resources, competent persons?
Are outputs identified and is traceability maintained where required?
Is property belonging to customers or external providers identified, verified, protected and safeguarded?
Are outputs preserved during production and delivery - handling, storage, packaging, protection?
Are post-delivery activities addressed, including statutory requirements and customer feedback?
Are changes to production reviewed and controlled, with records of the review and authorisation?
Is release of products and services verified against acceptance criteria, with evidence and authorisation?
Is nonconforming output identified, controlled and dispositioned, with records retained?
Is monitoring and measurement determined - what, by what method, when, and when results are analysed?
Is customer satisfaction monitored, with methods for obtaining and reviewing the information?
Are data analysed and evaluated to assess conformity, satisfaction, performance and external providers?
Are internal audits conducted at planned intervals by objective auditors, with results reported?
Is management review conducted at planned intervals covering all required inputs and outputs?
Are opportunities for improvement determined, selected and implemented?
Are nonconformities reacted to, root causes evaluated, action taken and effectiveness reviewed?
Is the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the QMS continually improved?
Are internal and external issues affecting environmental performance determined, including conditions?
Are interested parties, their needs and which become compliance obligations determined?
Is the EMS scope determined and available as documented information?
Is the environmental policy appropriate, committing to protection, compliance and continual improvement?
Are risks and opportunities relating to aspects, obligations and issues determined?
Are environmental aspects and impacts determined, with criteria used to identify significant aspects?
Are compliance obligations determined, accessible and taken into account in the EMS?
Is action planned to address significant aspects, obligations, risks and opportunities?
Are environmental objectives established at relevant functions, measurable and monitored?
Is competence for persons affecting environmental performance determined and evidenced?
Are persons aware of the policy, significant aspects and implications of not conforming?
Are internal and external environmental communications planned and carried out?
Is EMS documented information created, updated and controlled?
Are processes needed to meet EMS requirements planned, implemented and controlled, including outsourced?
Are emergency situations identified, with planned response, testing and periodic review?
Is environmental performance monitored, measured, analysed and evaluated with calibrated equipment?
Is compliance with obligations evaluated at a determined frequency, with knowledge of status maintained?
Are internal EMS audits conducted at planned intervals with results reported to management?
Does management review cover EMS status, aspects, obligations, objectives and performance?
Are environmental nonconformities corrected, causes evaluated and the EMS updated?
Is the EMS continually improved to enhance environmental performance?
Are internal and external issues relevant to OH&S performance determined?
Are workers and other interested parties and their needs determined, including legal requirements?
Is the OH&S management system scope determined and documented?
Does top management take overall responsibility for preventing work-related injury and ill health?
Does the OH&S policy commit to safe conditions, hazard elimination, consultation and improvement?
Are OH&S roles, responsibilities and authorities assigned and communicated at all levels?
Are workers consulted and participating at all applicable levels, with barriers removed?
Are risks and opportunities determined, taking account of hazards, legal requirements and workers?
Is hazard identification ongoing and proactive, covering routine, non-routine and emergency situations?
Are OH&S risks assessed using defined methodology and criteria, and applied proactively?
Are legal and other requirements determined, accessible, and kept up to date?
Is action planned to address hazards, risks, legal requirements and emergency preparedness?
Are OH&S objectives established, measurable, monitored, communicated and updated?
Are the resources needed for the OH&S management system determined and provided?
Is worker competence for hazard identification and safe work determined, provided and evaluated?
Are workers aware of the policy, hazards, incidents and their right to remove themselves from danger?
Is OH&S information communicated internally and externally, accounting for language and literacy?
Is OH&S documented information created, updated and controlled?
Are operational controls established, implemented and maintained to meet OH&S requirements?
Is the hierarchy of controls applied - eliminate, substitute, engineering, administrative, PPE?
Is change managed - new products, processes, equipment, legal changes and knowledge of hazards?
Is procurement controlled, including contractors and outsourced functions, to conform to the OH&SMS?
Is emergency preparedness planned, with response, periodic testing, training and communication?
Is OH&S performance monitored and measured, with criteria and calibrated equipment?
Is compliance with legal and other requirements evaluated and its status maintained?
Are internal OH&S audits conducted at planned intervals, with results reported to workers?
Does management review cover incidents, participation, hazards, risks, and adequacy of resources?
Are opportunities for improvement determined and improvement actions implemented?
Are incidents and nonconformities investigated, root causes determined and controls reviewed?
Is the OH&S management system continually improved, with worker participation?

footer_note: Retain with the internal audit report. Same checklist available live in Auditor Mode on the ISO portal.
print_rule: A blank form printed when needed. The completed sheet is the controlled record and is filed per its retention period. Blank printouts are not tracked as copies.
